anchors.quote: having like very relevant AI native skills uh in your CV
all you need to do is show people that you can leverage AI like code uh codeex cursor claude um to increase your output in in your developmental workflows

claim_en: Very relevant AI-native skills on the CV are very important now for all engineering: show that AI tools such as Codex, Cursor or Claude increase output in the development workflow.

anchors.quote: if they don't use AI at all if there's no mention of AI

claim_en: Asked which missing skill makes a JavaScript CV a reject, the recruiter names not using AI at all, no mention of AI.
notes: Answer to a question about skills whose absence leads to rejection; typed F, not F!, because the rejection is not stated for AI in the recruiter's own words.

anchors.quote: if I'm looking for a backend engineer and they don't mention mention nojs at all or they mention like PHP or something and I know my client uses TypeScript on the back end that that'll probably make me reject them instantly

claim_en: Hiring a backend engineer for a client with a TypeScript backend, the recruiter would probably reject instantly a CV with no Node.js or with PHP instead.

anchors.quote: I would always say tailor your CV and your skill sets to to the role
all of this depends on like the um job ad that you're applying to if the job ad says we we're looking for you know deep nodes JS internals then you know make that apparent
I would definitely tailor your CV um to to the job spec

claim_en: Always tailor the CV and skill set to the role; if the job ad stresses one area, make that apparent.

anchors.quote: if someone can do GCP or someone can do AWS they are quite interchangeable
what people tend to focus on is the core stack so the language the front-end framework and the backend framework

claim_en: Engineering leaders see AWS and GCP as quite interchangeable and focus on the core stack: the language and the frontend and backend frameworks.

anchors.quote: put your LinkedIn URL your GitHub URL if you're okay your contact number and the best email to reach you
just make sure you have the right you know uh right dial code

claim_en: On the CV put the LinkedIn URL, the GitHub URL if comfortable, a contact number with the right dial code and the best email.

anchors.quote: put your LinkedIn URL

anchors.quote: especially if you're applying direct if uh the internal recruiter wants to give you a call um you you know it is important that they know your number

claim_en: A mobile number is needed, especially when applying direct, so the internal recruiter can call.

anchors.quote: if I'm only hiring in the UK and I see you know someone from India someone from Germany uh it might not it might be a red flag

claim_en: Hiring only in the UK, the recruiter checks the phone number's country, and a foreign number might be a red flag.

anchors.quote: just try and avoid any u sort of um confusion um I guess the best thing that you can do is just write based in Germany or based in the UK on your CV

claim_en: Avoid confusion about location: write where you are based (for example based in the UK) on the CV and on LinkedIn.

anchors.quote: most recruiters uh will look at how like close your where you live is is to their office

claim_en: Most recruiters look at how close the candidate lives to their office.

anchors.quote: I would just say just be specific and just be just be truthful
just keep it specific you know maybe just name your city

claim_en: Be specific and truthful about location: name the actual city.

anchors.quote: they are offering sponsorship you you might put happy to relocate you know in your CV

claim_en: A candidate abroad applying where sponsorship is offered might put happy to relocate on the CV, so the recruiter knows they can move.

anchors.quote: I use LinkedIn I use welcome to the jungle and then I use cord as well

claim_en: The recruiter uses three job boards: LinkedIn, Welcome to the Jungle and Cord.

anchors.quote: if you work for Amazon then Google would probably want to hire you if you work for Amazon or bigger organization and you're looking to um apply for a startup it could actually end up hurting you that's why I think it's so important to put context in your CV
if you've worked on Greenfield project if you shipped fast then you know I I would still definitely give you a call

claim_en: A big-company background (Amazon) helps with other big companies but can hurt a startup application, because it suggests bureaucracy and a slower pace, unless the CV gives context such as a startup-like team, greenfield work or shipping fast.

anchors.quote: universities definitely definitely include
even if your education is not computer science I would I would definitely include it as well as sort of you know what score you got
especially if you got like a merit or distinction I'd definitely put that in there

claim_en: Definitely include good universities, even when the degree is not computer science, with the score, especially a merit or distinction.

anchors.quote: make sure there's no misinformation on there
if the recruiter then asks you about a specific line on your CV and you actually haven't done it it it's almost an instant no right because you've broken that trust

claim_en: Check that everything on the CV is accurate, since AI can add things not done: if the recruiter asks about a line the candidate has not done, it is almost an instant rejection because trust is broken.

anchors.quote: we work with companies that do offer sponsorship um so and they also offer relocation fees uh for exceptional candidates
nine times out of 10 the remote the EU remote roles are are sort of um you know um more popular

claim_en: Some client companies offer sponsorship and relocation fees for exceptional candidates, but EU remote roles are far more common in the market right now.

anchors.quote: that's going to make a big difference
I think it really puts you on the top of the pile

claim_en: A referral from an engineer at the company makes a big difference and puts the candidate at the top of the pile.

anchors.quote: management referrals are very important as well
one candidate already has their managerial referrals and numbers and emails attached

claim_en: Have managers' references (with numbers and emails) ready: between two equal finalists, the one with references attached may get the job.

anchors.quote: if you are applying for a UK startup at least have good enough English where you can understand sort of the technical requirements

claim_en: For a UK startup, have English good enough to understand the technical requirements and the product direction; communication matters because the team is close to customers and stakeholders.
